key_insight: The paper extends Fourier analysis to amplitude-embedded variational quantum circuits and shows that their Fourier coefficients concentrate near zero with variance that decays exponentially with frequency magnitude, revealing how non-linear data embedding shapes expressivity and trainability.
engineering_relevance: This gives quantum algorithm designers a practical framework to predict function expressivity and barren-plateau behavior for amplitude-encoded models, including how noise further suppresses learnable signal on hardware.
method: Analyzed amplitude embedding with a careful distinction in input-domain handling that changes the zero-frequency coefficient.
Used 2-design assumptions and Weingarten calculus to derive mean and variance scaling of Fourier coefficients.
Extended the analysis to noisy channels with unitary Kraus operators, showing an additional variance reduction factor.
evidence_signal: The authors validate the theory with simulations in both noiseless and noisy settings, including target functions decomposed into non-integer frequencies.
watch_item: The strongest guarantees rely on the unitary ensemble behaving at least like a 2-design and on a specific noise model, so results may weaken for less structured circuits or more general device noise.
paper_title: Fourier analysis of quantum neural network with non-linear data embedding
